section.description: Questions based only on the transcript provided for this 30-second section.

question_pattern.descriptive_evaluation: The learner may answer in their own words. Compare the learner answer with the reference answer using cosine similarity.
question_pattern.sequence_test: After the main questions, ask multiple-choice questions that test whether the learner remembers the events in the correct order.

questions.question: How long was the original presentation that the speaker usually gives to high school students?
questions.answer_text: The original presentation was two hours long.

questions.question: Where did the story that led to this presentation begin?
questions.answer_text: The story began one day on a plane while the speaker was traveling to TED.

questions.question: Who was sitting next to the speaker on the plane?
questions.answer_text: A high school student, who was a teenager, was sitting next to the speaker.

questions.question: What did the speaker say about the student's family?

options.A: She came from a very wealthy family.
options.B: She came from a famous family.
options.C: She came from a really poor family.

questions.answer_text: The student came from a really poor family.

questions.question: What question did the student ask the speaker?

options.A: How can I become a TED speaker?
options.D: Why do people go to TED?

questions.question: Why do you think the student wanted to make something of her life?
questions.reference_answer: The student came from a really poor family, but she wanted to improve her life and become successful.

questions.question: Why did the speaker feel bad when the student asked what leads to success?
questions.reference_answer: The speaker felt bad because he could not give the student a good answer to her question about what leads to success.

sequence_test.description: These questions test whether the learner understood the events in the correct order. The learner should watch the complete section before answering.

questions.question: What happened first?

options.C: The speaker met a high school student on a plane.

questions.answer_text: The speaker first met the high school student on the plane.

questions.question: What happened after the speaker met the student on the plane?

options.A: She asked him what leads to success.

questions.answer_text: The student wanted to make something of her life and asked what leads to success.

questions.question: What did the speaker do after arriving at TED?

options.B: He decided to ask successful people what helped them succeed.
options.C: He asked the student another question.

questions.answer_text: After arriving at TED, he decided to ask successful people what helped them succeed and pass that information on to kids.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly describes the main events?

options.A: TED → student → plane → success question → interviews
options.B: Plane → student → success question → TED → ask successful people
options.C: Student → TED → success question → plane → interviews
options.D: Success question → plane → TED → student → interviews

questions.answer_text: The speaker was on a plane, met the student, heard her question about success, went to TED, and decided to ask successful people what helped them succeed.

descriptive.description: Create embeddings for the learner's answer and the reference answer, then calculate cosine similarity.
descriptive.note: Cosine similarity should be treated as an aid rather than the only measure of correctness.
